quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a divided road, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection carefully without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Go when it is safe.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need a longer distance to stop than small cars.
Need less time to pass going downhill than small cars.
Turn in a smaller space than small cars.
Need less time to pass going uphill than small cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need a longer distance to stop than small cars.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more space to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Stay farther away from that vehicle.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Not drive the same way as that driver.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If you see a driver who is not paying attention, give them extra space. A distracted driver is more likely to crash.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer gets to your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time you drive.
questions.explanation: All people in a car should wear seat belts every time. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and can hurt others.

questions.question: Driving ability can be hurt by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical health. Alcohol, drugs, and being tired all hurt your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: A seat belt should be fitted so it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Keeps the belt warning light from coming on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check blind spots when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from the curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change where your car is on the road. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal in the direction you want to go. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in that direction. Make sure no one else is moving into that lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead of you.
Drive with caution around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between your vehicle and others because wet, cold roads are slippery. Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on these surfaces.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut off the other driver to get back at them.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, cross multiple lanes at the last second, or cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When should you always signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Continue driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles with sirens, air horns, or flashing lights pass. Pull over to the right side of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. When the lead vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession may follow through, even if the traffic light is red.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination could increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination could increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol with other drugs can increase how much both affect you. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: If someone has consumed alcohol, what will help them overcome its effects?
questions.explanation: Only time will allow the body to overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no warning signals, should you slow down, look, and listen?
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings without warning devices, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger signals you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: What is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place infants or small children in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt infants and small children, even in minor crashes.
Make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and require all passengers to use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts reduce injury and death in crashes. Children 12 and under must ride properly restrained in the back seat. Never place rear-facing infant seats in the front seat of vehicles with airbags.

questions.question: Is the most common backing mistake failing to look both ways behind the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Most drivers fail to look both ways when backing. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to look through the rear window.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop immediately after an accident. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Call the police and an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding but do not move injured people. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a driver?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows brain activity and reduces safe driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Does a "Merging lanes" sign mean you should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into your lane?
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes going the same way will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What is true about signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb?

options.text: You only need to signal if other traffic is nearby.
It is good practice and required by law.
You only need to signal during the maneuver, not before.
You do not need to signal if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before you move left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, what should you do?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slick roads are always dangerous. Turns and curves are especially risky. Slow down for turns on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Trains may be crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus on the road. Any extra activity takes your attention away from driving. This makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycles have the right of way.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep tire tread in good condition and tire pressure at the right level. Drive slower in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot go this way from your direction. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what is important to do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Signal before changing lanes. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before moving.

questions.question: What should a driver taking over-the-counter medicine do?

options.text: Drive anyway, even if there are warnings.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings. If unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Wait in your car for help.
Honk your horn at other drivers.
Flash your headlights at oncoming cars.

questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road safely and park where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to show your car is broken down.
